abilities.name: Blazing Blessing

_curatorNotes: Refresh semantics: a new Blazing Barrier stacks the REMAINING absorption of the existing one and refreshes duration, capped at the 'Max Shield DMG Absorption' row (35.3% Max HP + 4153 @T10). Cap not modelled; durationType 'refresh' captures the timing side only.

Target 'active': the barrier protects whoever is on-field (standard party shield; A1 kit text refers to 'your current active character obtains ... a Blazing Barrier'). Absorbs Pyro DMG 250% more effectively — not modelled.
effects.label: Blazing Barrier

abilities.description:
Thoma vaults forward with his polearm and delivers a flame-filled flying kick that deals AoE Pyro DMG, while also summoning a defensive Blazing Barrier. At the moment of casting, Thoma's Elemental Skill applies Pyro to himself.
The DMG Absorption of the Blazing Barrier scales off Thoma's Max HP.
The Blazing Barrier has the following traits:
·Absorbs Pyro DMG 250% more effectively.
·When a new Blazing Barrier is obtained, the remaining DMG Absorption of an existing Blazing Barrier will stack and its duration will be refreshed.

The maximum DMG Absorption of the Blazing Barrier will not exceed a certain percentage of Thoma's Max HP.
_curatorNotes: ↻ 2026-08-14 — the stand-in summon is retired. "Blazing Barrier" was a zero-effect `summons[]` entry whose only jobs were to give this instant cast a 8s active window and to put a labelled bar on the chart. Both now have their own field: `activeDuration` on the ability and `label` on the shield Effect, which the shield lane renders. `summons[]` is back to meaning a thing left in the world. Bar geometry is unchanged apart from the spawn offset, which the shield window never had.

abilities.name: Crimson Ooyoroi

_curatorNotes: Coordinated attack, authored 2026-08-18. gcsim thoma/thoma.go:43 registers a minazuki.Watcher on action.NormalAttackState with tickerFreq 60 and a 60f ICD key, firing summonFieryCollapse (burst.go) — ONE hit at travel 11, Pyro, Durability 25, ICDTagElementalBurst/ICDGroupDefault. Talent row 'Fiery Collapse DMG' = 104.4% ATK at level 10.

⚠️ icdGate is ABSENT on purpose: the wave is a single hit on gcsim's DEFAULT group, which is what absent already means, and icd.md forbids annotating the default. Consequence, and it is the game's: waves land every second and Pyro applies on every third — Thoma applies once per ~3s, not once per second.
procCooldown 1 = the in-kit 'Fiery Collapse can be triggered once every 1s' ICD (kit text; matches gcsim burstICDKey 60-frame ICD).

trigger source 'team': any party member's Normal Attacks proc it — only the active character can normal attack, matching the kit's 'the active character's Normal Attacks'. Charged/plunging attacks do NOT proc it.

Only live while Scorching Ooyoroi is active (15s summon, +3s at C2). No explicit duringSummon condition, mirroring the traveler_electro burst onHit precedent — burst-hosted onHit effects scope to the burst window.

Refresh semantics: each proc stacks remaining absorption of an existing Blazing Barrier and refreshes its 8s duration; capped by Blazing Blessing's 'Max Shield DMG Absorption' row (35.3% Max HP + 4153 @T10). Cap and cross-ability stacking not modelled.

Fiery Collapse shield authored on this ability (see effects[]). Fiery Collapse DAMAGE (58%..137.75% ATK AoE Pyro per proc, 104.4% @T10) not yet authored — needs reviewer pass; would be a `damage` effect with the same onHit trigger, plus the A4 +2.2% Max HP FlatDmg rider (see thoma__passive__flaming_assault). gcsim: `summonFieryCollapse()` via burst.go with burstICDKey 60-frame ICD.
abilities.description:
Thoma spins his polearm, slicing at his foes with roaring flames that deal AoE Pyro DMG and weave themselves into a Scorching Ooyoroi.

Scorching Ooyoroi
While Scorching Ooyoroi is in effect, the active character's Normal Attacks will trigger Fiery Collapse, dealing AoE Pyro DMG and summoning a Blazing Barrier.
Fiery Collapse can be triggered once every 1s.

Except for the amount of DMG they can absorb, the Blazing Barriers created in this way are identical to those created by Thoma's Elemental Skill, Blazing Blessing:
·Absorbs Pyro DMG 250% more effectively.
·When a new Blazing Barrier is obtained, the remaining DMG Absorption of an existing Blazing Barrier will stack and its duration will be refreshed.

The maximum DMG Absorption of the Blazing Barrier will not exceed a certain percentage of Thoma's Max HP.

If Thoma falls, the effects of Scorching Ooyoroi will be cleared.

passives.name: Flaming Assault
passives.description: DMG dealt by Crimson Ooyoroi's Fiery Collapse is increased by 2.2% of Thoma's Max HP.
_curatorNotes: ↻ 2026-09-21 (manual-trigger retirement, docs/manual-trigger-retirement-round.md). CONVERTED from `damage`/`manual` to the flat-DMG house form. gcsim `asc.go:30-34` returns `0.022 × MaxHP` and `burst.go:90` uses it as `FlatDmg` on the `summonFieryCollapse` AttackInfo — an addend on an existing hit, never its own attack. ⚠️ Crimson Ooyoroi's own cast hit (`burst.go:29-47`) is also `AttackTagElementalBurst` and carries NO `FlatDmg`, so `burstFlatDmg` is broader than the kit by that one hit; taken anyway because it is precisely what the house form already does (Cyno's A4 names "Duststalker Bolt DMG" and is authored `skillFlatDmg` beside his own skill hit), and the visible cost is a stat name on the always-on chip, never a printed damage number. ⚠️ gcsim's guard reads `Ascension < 1`, an upstream typo; the talent is A4.

_curatorNotes: CD reduction effect not yet authored — needs reviewer pass. Conditional: triggers when a character protected by Thoma's Blazing Barrier is attacked; reduces E and Q CD by 3s each. ICD: once per 20s. Externally-triggered (enemy attack on shielded ally), not a standard `onCast`/`onHit`. gcsim simplifies by setting base CD to 12s/17s at C1.
constellations.description:
When a character protected by Thoma's own Blazing Barrier (Thoma excluded) is attacked, Thoma's own Blazing Blessing CD is decreased by 3s, while his own Crimson Ooyoroi's CD is decreased by 3s.
This effect can be triggered once every 20s.

notModeled.reason: This triggers when an opponent attacks a shielded character, and we don't model incoming attacks.
